metaDescription: Commercial interior holiday decor for lobbies, atriums and reception areas across Ontario. Designed, installed, serviced, removed and stored by one crew.
h1: Interior holiday decor for lobbies, atriums and reception areas
intro: Commercial Holiday Decorators is a commercial interior holiday decor company based in London, Ontario. We design, supply, install, maintain and remove holiday decor for office lobbies, hotel atriums, condo entrances, reception areas and elevator lobbies across Southwestern Ontario, the GTA and Hamilton-Niagara. Everything you see is our own inventory, which is why we can stand behind it for the whole season.

An interior program usually starts with a decorated pre-lit tree sized to the ceiling, then builds out from there: lit garland on staircases and railings, an entrance arch, wreaths on glass, planters at the doors and ornament accents at the reception desk. Colour schemes are matched to your brand or your interior finishes, so the decor looks like it belongs in the building rather than dropped into it.

The work happens after hours or overnight so tenants, guests and deliveries are not disrupted. Our crews are insured and WSIB-compliant, trees are secured against tipping, and every power connection runs on a timer. If anything fails during the season we fix it at no charge. In January we take it all down, label it and store it in our warehouse for next year.

includes.title: Design and colour scheme
includes.body: We visit the space, measure ceiling heights, note the finishes and propose a scheme that fits. Gold and warm white suits marble and granite lobbies; navy and silver works against glass and steel. You get photos and a written scope before anything is ordered, so the board or the GM can approve a specific look.

includes.title: Decorated pre-lit trees
includes.body: Commercial-grade pre-lit trees from 7 to 20+ ft, fully decorated with ribbon, ornaments and toppers before you arrive in the morning. Trees are weighted and secured, lights are LED and the plug runs to a timer. Atrium trees over 12 ft are assembled from a lift with a two-person crew.

includes.title: Garland, arches and railings
includes.body: Lit garland along staircase railings, across reception desks, over elevator banks and around entrance vestibules. We build walk-through garland arches over glass doors where the structure allows. Attachments use clips and ties that leave no marks on stone, wood or glass, and nothing blocks a door closer or an exit sign.

includes.title: Planters, wreaths and accents
includes.body: Urns and planters at the doors dressed with evergreen, birch, lit branches and ribbon. Wreaths on glass walls and over entrances, lit gift boxes beside elevators, ornament clusters at the desk. These are the pieces that make the lobby read as finished from every angle, including the security camera.

includes.title: Themed and custom displays
includes.body: For larger atriums and hotels we build custom themed displays: light tunnels, sleigh features, reindeer sculptures, lit birch forests and photo moments. We design around traffic flow and fire code, keep every piece on a timer and leave you a plan showing where each element sits so security knows what to expect.

includes.title: Season service, takedown and storage
includes.body: A bulb out, a ribbon pulled loose by a stroller, a tree nudged by a mover: we come back and fix it at no charge. In the first three weeks of January we remove everything, inventory it by location, label it and store it in our climate-controlled warehouse. Your dates are held for next season.

process.title: Site visit and measurements
process.body: Between July and September we walk the lobby with you, measure clearances, check power locations and photograph the sightlines from the entrance, the elevators and the street. Buildings outside our daily range can send plans and photos to start.

process.title: Design, scope and quote
process.body: You receive a written scope with tree sizes, garland footage, planter counts and reference photos, priced for one season or a multi-year term. We note any lift access or after-hours security requirements so there are no surprises on install night.

process.title: Overnight installation
process.body: Installs run October through late November, scheduled with your concierge or property manager for after hours. A typical lobby program is complete in one night. We bring the lift, the protection for your floors and our own extension cords and timers.

process.title: Service, takedown and storage
process.body: We check in through the season and respond to any fault at no charge. Takedown happens in January on a date you choose. Everything is labelled and stored in our warehouse so next year's install starts from a known inventory.

faqs.question: What does a commercial interior holiday decor program typically cost?
faqs.answer: Pricing is custom from a site visit or from plans and photos. As a typical range, a lobby tree program commonly starts around $1,500 per season for a 9 ft decorated tree and runs into five figures for full atrium and hotel programs with garland, planters and themed displays. The main drivers are tree count and height, garland footage, lift requirements and whether you commit to one season or a multi-year term.

faqs.question: Do you install decor that we already own?
faqs.answer: No. We install only our own commercial-grade inventory, because that is the only way we can warranty it and keep a spare on the truck when a strand fails. If you have existing decor you want to keep using, we can design around it in the same space, but we will not hang, wire or maintain product we did not supply. Most clients who switch to our program find the lease covers more than their old purchase did.

faqs.question: How do you handle power, timers and fire code in a lobby?
faqs.answer: Every tree and garland run plugs into a timer we supply, set to your building hours, so nothing is left on overnight unless you want it. We use LED product with low draw, avoid daisy-chaining past the rated limit and keep cords out of walkways with covers or routing behind planters. Nothing is attached to sprinkler heads, exit signs, door closers or fire equipment, and we keep required clearances around pull stations.

faqs.question: Can you install without disrupting tenants or guests?
faqs.answer: Yes. Interior installs are scheduled after hours or overnight with your concierge, security or property manager. We protect floors, work from our own lifts and ladders, and leave the lobby clean before the first person arrives in the morning. Most lobby programs are complete in a single night. Larger atrium displays may take two nights, and we tell you that in the quote.

faqs.question: What happens if something fails or gets damaged during the season?
faqs.answer: Call or text us and we come back and fix it at no charge, whether it is a bulb section out on a tree, ribbon pulled loose, a planter knocked by a delivery cart or a timer that lost its program after a power blip. Maintenance is included on every program. Because we own the inventory we carry spares, so a repair is usually a swap, not a wait for parts.

ctaBody: Site visits and design run July through September and early bookings get first pick of install dates. Call 519-266-6796 or send photos and a floor plan and we will reply within one business day with a scope and price.

metaDescription: Commercial Christmas light installation in Ontario: rooflines, canopies, columns, tree wrapping and parking-lot trees. Insured crews, lifts, full service.
h1: Commercial Christmas light installation for buildings, trees and grounds
intro: Commercial Christmas light installation is the core of what we do outdoors: building outlines and rooflines, porte-cochère and canopy lighting, lit columns and entrances, tree wrapping, cone trees, hedges, walkways, boulevards and parking-lot trees. We have lit commercial properties across Southwestern Ontario, the GTA and Hamilton-Niagara since 2016, from a single storefront to multi-building campuses and downtown streetscapes. Everything we hang is our own commercial-grade inventory.

We use commercial-grade LED strings and C9 bulbs on our own clips and stock, so the product survives Ontario wind, ice and snow load without failing in week two. Crews work from bucket trucks and aerial lifts, which means rooflines three and four storeys up and mature boulevard trees are in scope, not just what a ladder reaches. That reach also means fewer ladders on your property and a faster night.

Installs are scheduled after hours or overnight so parking, deliveries and customers are not disrupted, and every circuit runs on a timer or photocell. If a strand goes out, a clip lets go in a storm or a plow clips a cone tree, we fix it at no charge. January takedown, labelled storage and priority dates next season are part of every program.

includes.title: Rooflines and building outlines
includes.body: C9 LED bulbs or commercial mini lights along eaves, parapets, gables and ridgelines so the building reads from the road. We measure the linear footage, pick the clip for your edge detail (shingle, flashing, metal fascia, stone) and run the feed to a protected outlet on a timer. Multi-storey rooflines are installed from a lift.

includes.title: Porte-cochères, canopies and columns
includes.body: Entrance canopies, drive-through porte-cochères and the columns that carry them are where guests and tenants actually stand. We outline the canopy edge, wrap or garland the columns and add wreaths at the drop-off so the arrival moment is lit. Clearance for delivery trucks and coach height is checked before anything is hung.

includes.title: Tree wrapping
includes.body: Trunk and branch wrapping on deciduous and evergreen trees at entrances, along boulevards and across courtyards, in warm white or colours. Mature trees are wrapped from a lift so the canopy is lit, not just the first eight feet. Wraps are tied off so growth and wind do not cut into bark.

includes.title: Cone trees, hedges and landscape
includes.body: Lit cone trees in beds and along frontage, hedges and shrubs wrapped or netted, walkways and planters lit at ground level. Cone trees are staked against wind and set back from plow lines. Landscape lighting in blue or warm white adds depth under the roofline work without adding much to the power load.

includes.title: Parking lots and boulevard trees
includes.body: Rows of parking-lot evergreens, median cone trees and street-tree wrapping along the frontage. These runs need traffic management, lift positioning and a power plan that often uses lamp-post receptacles or dedicated weatherproof feeds. We handle the layout, the cones and the overnight scheduling so the lot stays open by day.

includes.title: Power, timers and season service
includes.body: We map every circuit before install, split loads so no breaker is near its limit and put each feed on a timer or photocell set to your hours. Weatherproof connections are taped and elevated off the ground. Faults during the season are fixed at no charge, including after storms, and takedown and storage follow in January.

process.title: Site visit and power survey
process.body: We walk the property between July and September, measure rooflines and tree sizes, locate exterior outlets and lamp-post receptacles, check lift access and note where coach or truck clearance matters. Remote sites can start from photos and a site plan.

process.title: Design and quote
process.body: You receive a written scope with footage, tree counts, colour choices and lift requirements, priced per season or on a multi-year agreement that locks the price and the dates. We flag any electrical work your electrician should handle before we arrive.

process.title: Overnight installation
process.body: Crews install October through late November so the property is lit before Black Friday. Work runs after hours with bucket trucks and lifts, cones and spotters for traffic, and a final timer check before we leave the site.

process.title: Service, takedown and storage
process.body: Any fault is fixed at no charge through the season, with storm checks after major wind or ice. Takedown runs the first three weeks of January. Product is inventoried, labelled by location and stored in our warehouse for your next install.

faqs.question: How much does commercial Christmas light installation cost in Ontario?
faqs.answer: It is quoted from a site visit or from photos and a site plan. As a typical range, exterior programs start from a few thousand dollars for a storefront roofline and entrance, and run to tens of thousands for a plaza, campus or multi-building property with tree wrapping and parking-lot trees. Linear footage, tree count and size, lift requirements and one-season versus multi-year are the price drivers. These are typical ranges, not quotes.

faqs.question: Do you need power on the roof or can you run from ground outlets?
faqs.answer: Most rooflines run from existing exterior outlets, with feeds routed up a downspout or column and secured. We map circuits before install so no single breaker carries more than it should and keep connections weatherproofed and off the ground. Lamp-post receptacles work well for parking-lot and boulevard trees. If a property has no suitable outlet where we need it, we tell you in the quote so your electrician can add a weatherproof GFCI before install.

faqs.question: How do you keep lights working through wind, ice and snow?
faqs.answer: We use commercial-grade LED product on purpose-made clips rather than consumer strings and zip ties, tie off tree wraps so they do not slide, stake cone trees and keep connections elevated and taped. Each circuit sits on a timer or photocell. After a major storm we check the property, and anything that has come loose or gone dark is fixed at no charge. That service is part of every program, not an add-on.

faqs.question: Can you install without closing the parking lot or blocking the entrance?
faqs.answer: Yes. Exterior installs are scheduled after hours or overnight, when the lot is empty and the entrance is quiet. We bring cones and a spotter for lift work near traffic and keep fire lanes and loading areas clear. Porte-cochère work is timed around check-in and deliveries. By the time the first customer or tenant arrives, the lift is gone and the lights are set to come on that evening.

faqs.question: What happens to the lights in January?
faqs.answer: We take everything down in the first three weeks of January, including the clips, cords and timers, and leave the building as we found it. Product is inventoried, labelled by location and stored in our warehouse, where it is tested and refurbished before next season. Your install dates are held as a returning client. If you own the product rather than lease it, the same takedown and storage service applies under your annual program.

ctaTitle: Get your property lit before Black Friday
ctaBody: Install dates fill from October onward and early bookings get first pick. Call 519-266-6796 or send photos of the building and grounds and we will respond within one business day with a scope and price.

h1: Lobby Christmas tree rental and setup
intro: Lobby Christmas tree rental and setup is the simplest way for a building to look finished for the season without owning, storing or assembling anything. We deliver a commercial-grade pre-lit tree sized to your ceiling, decorate it on site in your colour scheme, secure it, put it on a timer and come back in January to remove it. The tree lives in our warehouse the other eleven months.

Trees run from 7 ft for a reception corner to 20+ ft for an atrium or hotel lobby. All are pre-lit with warm-white or coloured LED, then dressed with ribbon, ornaments, picks and a topper chosen to match your finishes or brand. Elevator-lobby and reception trees often pair with lit gift boxes and planters so the whole floor reads as one design.

Setup happens after hours or overnight so tenants and guests never see a half-built tree. Trees over 12 ft go up with a lift and a two-person crew. Maintenance is included: if a light section fails or a stroller pulls a ribbon loose, we fix it at no charge. Leasing is our default recommendation for lobby trees, and the FAQ below explains why.

includes.title: Tree sized to the space
includes.body: We measure ceiling height, the footprint you can give up and the sightline from the entrance before recommending a size. A 9 ft tree suits most office and condo lobbies; 12 to 16 ft fills a double-height entrance; 20+ ft is for atriums and hotel lobbies. Width matters as much as height for traffic flow.

includes.title: Pre-lit commercial-grade tree
includes.body: Our trees are commercial grade with dense tips and factory-wired LED lighting that is tested before it leaves the warehouse. Warm white is standard; coloured and multi-tone options are available. The lighting is wired in sections so a fault affects one section, and we carry replacements on the truck.

includes.title: Full decoration in your scheme
includes.body: Ribbon, shatterproof ornaments, picks, florals and a topper, placed by our crew on site. Gold and warm white for marble lobbies, navy and silver for glass and steel, red and gold for traditional interiors, or your brand colours. Ornaments are wired on, not hooked, so they survive the season.

includes.title: Secured, powered and on a timer
includes.body: Trees are set on a weighted base and, where height requires, tied off discreetly to prevent tipping in a busy lobby. The plug runs to a timer we supply, set to your building hours. Cords are routed under covers or behind the skirt so there is nothing to trip on.

includes.title: Accent trees, gift boxes and planters
includes.body: A tall tree flanked by two lit accent trees is the classic lobby composition. Lit gift boxes beside elevators, matching planters at the doors and a wreath on the glass finish the floor. These pieces are quoted as add-ons so you can build the program up over a few seasons.

includes.title: Removal, refurbishment and storage
includes.body: In the first three weeks of January we remove the tree and decor, inventory the ornaments and ribbon by building, and store everything in our climate-controlled warehouse. Trees are tested and refurbished before next season. Your install date is held as a returning client.

process.body: A quick site visit or a few photos with ceiling height is enough to size the tree and propose a scheme. We note elevator or stair access for the delivery, power location and where the lift can set up if the tree is tall.

process.title: Approve the look
process.body: You get a written scope with tree height, colour scheme, accent pieces and reference photos, priced per season or on a multi-year term. Boards and GMs can approve a specific design rather than a vague line item.

process.title: Overnight setup
process.body: We deliver, assemble, decorate and clean up in one after-hours visit for most lobbies. Tall atrium trees take a lift and a second night. Lights are tested, the timer is set and we photograph the finished tree for your records.

process.title: Service and January removal
process.body: Any issue through the season is fixed at no charge. In January we remove the tree on a date you choose, usually before the 21st, and store it labelled in our warehouse for next year.

faqs.question: How much does lobby Christmas tree rental and setup cost?
faqs.answer: Programs are quoted per season from a site visit or photos. As a typical range, a 9 ft fully decorated pre-lit tree with delivery, setup, maintenance, removal and storage commonly starts around $1,500 per season. Taller trees, accent trees, gift boxes and planters add to that, and 16 to 20+ ft atrium trees with lift installation run well into the thousands. Multi-year agreements lock the price. These are typical figures, not quotes.

faqs.question: Should we lease a lobby tree or buy one?
faqs.answer: For most buildings, leasing wins. You pay one seasonal price that covers the tree, decoration, setup, maintenance, removal and storage, with no capital purchase, no storage room given up and no staff time assembling branches. Buying makes sense only if you have dry storage and expect to run the same tree for many years; you still pay annually for setup, service and takedown. We explain both honestly in the quote.

faqs.question: Can a 20 ft tree get into our lobby?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes. Tall trees are built in sections on site, so the question is lift access and ceiling height, not door width. We check the route from the loading dock, the elevator cab size for the sections and where a lift can set up on your floor. If the lobby cannot take a lift, we build with ladders and scaffold where safe. We confirm all of this during the site visit before quoting.

faqs.question: What if the lights on the tree fail mid-season?
faqs.answer: Call or text and we come out and fix it at no charge. Our trees are wired in sections, so a fault usually takes out one band of lights rather than the whole tree, and we carry replacement sections and plugs on the truck. The same applies to ribbon, ornaments or a tree that has been nudged by a mover. Maintenance is included on every rental program for the full season.

faqs.question: Do you install trees we already own?
faqs.answer: No. We only set up trees and decor from our own inventory so we can warranty the lights, replace sections on the spot and store everything properly in January. Customer-owned trees often have mixed-age lighting and no spare parts, which turns a service call into a guessing game. If you already own a tree, compare its annual setup and storage effort against a lease price; most buildings find the lease is simpler and looks better.

ctaTitle: Reserve a lobby tree for this season
ctaBody: Tell us the ceiling height and send a photo of the lobby. We will reply within one business day with a tree size, a colour scheme and a per-season price. Call 519-266-6796 or use the form.

metaDescription: Lit wreaths, garland and dressed planters for commercial entrances, railings and canopies across Ontario. Supplied, installed, serviced and stored.
h1: Wreaths, garland and planters for commercial entrances
intro: Wreaths, garland and planters are what turn a lit building into a decorated one. A lit wreath over the entrance, garland wrapped on the columns and along the canopy edge, and a pair of dressed urns at the doors give a commercial property a finished look at the exact point where people walk in. We supply, install, service and store all of it as part of a seasonal program.

Our garland is commercial-grade artificial evergreen with built-in LED lighting, wired for outdoor use and dense enough to look full from the street. Wreaths run from 24 inches for a door to 6 ft and larger for a facade or gable. Bows and ribbon are weatherproof and wired, so they hold their shape through December wind rather than drooping by the second week.

Indoors, the same pieces move to staircases, reception desks, elevator banks and vestibules. We attach with clips, ties and stands that leave no marks on stone, glass, wood or metal and never block a door closer, exit sign or sprinkler. Any fault during the season is fixed at no charge, and everything comes down and goes into labelled storage in January.

includes.title: Entrance and facade wreaths
includes.body: Lit wreaths over doors, on gables, on columns and along balconies, sized to the opening and hung on mounts that suit brick, stucco, glass or metal. Larger wreaths on a facade are installed from a lift and secured against wind. Each wreath is wired to the nearest circuit on a timer or photocell.

includes.title: Lit garland on railings and staircases
includes.body: Garland wrapped along exterior railings, interior staircases and mezzanine edges with lights running the full length. We space the wrap so handrails stay usable and the attachment points do not scratch finishes. Gold poinsettia, pinecone and ribbon accents can be added to match a lobby scheme.

includes.title: Columns and canopies
includes.body: Garland spiralled on entrance columns and run along porte-cochère and canopy edges, with wreaths centred between columns. This is the most-photographed part of many hotels and plazas, so we check it from the approach road, the drop-off and the lobby looking out before calling it done.

includes.title: Urns and planters
includes.body: Existing urns and planters dressed with evergreen, birch poles, red dogwood, lit branches, magnolia and ribbon, built on a base that handles freeze-thaw. We can supply planters where you have none. Arrangements are secured so a gust across a plaza does not scatter them, and lit branches sit on the same timer as the entrance.

includes.title: Bows, ribbon and accents
includes.body: Weatherproof wired ribbon in your scheme on wreaths, garland swags, lamp posts and planters. Bows are tied by hand and wired in place rather than stapled, so they can be removed, stored flat and reused. Colour is matched to the roofline and tree lighting so the whole frontage reads as one design.

includes.title: Service, takedown and storage
includes.body: If a bow blows loose, a wreath section goes dark or a planter is knocked by a snowplow, we fix or replace it at no charge. In January we remove everything, store garland on reels and wreaths on racks in our warehouse, and refurbish bows and lighting before the next season.

faqs.question: Can wreaths and garland be added to an existing lighting program?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is how most properties grow their display. Year one is often the roofline and a lobby tree; year two adds entrance wreaths, column garland and planters. Because we store your inventory and hold your install dates, additions are quoted as a line on the same program and installed on the same night. We match the ribbon and light colour to what is already there so nothing looks bolted on.

faqs.question: How do you attach garland and wreaths without damaging the building?
faqs.answer: We choose the mount for the surface: masonry clips and existing anchor points for brick and stone, suction and edge mounts for glass, wrapped ties for railings and columns, and magnetic or clip mounts on metal fascia. We do not drill into finishes without written approval. Nothing attaches to sprinkler heads, exit signs, door closers or security cameras, and handrails stay usable with the garland in place.

faqs.question: Will the planters survive freeze and thaw?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arrangements are built in a base that drains and does not crack when the soil freezes, and stems are anchored so they stay upright through a thaw. Lit branches use outdoor-rated LED on the same timer as the entrance. If a plow or a cart knocks a planter over, call us and we reset or rebuild it at no charge as part of your seasonal maintenance.

faqs.question: Do you provide real or artificial greenery?
faqs.answer: Our garland and wreaths are commercial-grade artificial evergreen with built-in LED lighting. Artificial product stays green and lit from early November through January without drying out, shedding or becoming a fire concern indoors, and it goes into storage and comes back next year, which is what makes a multi-year program affordable. Planter arrangements can include fresh-cut accents where a client wants them.

faqs.question: What happens if a bow or a section of garland fails during the season?
faqs.answer: You call or text us and we come out and fix it, replace it or re-tie it at no charge. We carry spare garland sections, bows and plugs on the truck, so most calls are a single visit. Entrances are also checked after major wind or ice storms without you having to ask. Maintenance is included in every program, whether you lease the decor or own it under an annual service agreement.

ctaBody: Send a photo of your entrance and we will reply within one business day with wreath sizes, garland footage and a price, on its own or added to your lighting program. Call 519-266-6796 to talk it through.

metaDescription: Turnkey commercial Christmas decor leasing: one seasonal price for design, product, install, service, removal and storage. Multi-year terms lock pricing.
h1: Turnkey holiday decor leasing for commercial properties
intro: Turnkey commercial Christmas decor leasing means you pay one seasonal price and we handle everything else: design, the product itself, installation, maintenance all season, January removal and storage in our warehouse until next year. You never own, store, repair or assemble anything. It is the model we recommend by default for lobby trees, atrium programs and large exterior displays. There is no capital purchase and no storage room lost.

The alternative is to buy the product and pay for the service program each year. That can make sense for a long-running, unchanging program where you have dry storage space, but it front-loads cost and leaves you holding inventory that ages. Leasing spreads cost evenly, keeps the display fresh and means a failed strand is our problem, not a line in your capital budget.

Multi-year agreements lock pricing and install dates for the term, which matters when budgets are approved a year ahead and install slots before Black Friday fill early. Everything we lease is our own commercial-grade inventory, which is why maintenance is included at no charge. Insured, WSIB-compliant crews do the work after hours or overnight. Property managers running several sites get one contact and one invoice for the whole portfolio.

faqs.question: What does turnkey holiday decor leasing include?
faqs.answer: One seasonal price covers the design and site visit, the decor itself, installation by insured crews after hours, maintenance all season with no charge for any fault, removal in January and storage in our warehouse until next year. Timers, cords, lifts and labour are all in. The only thing you supply is power and access. There are no separate rental, delivery or service invoices through the season.

faqs.question: Is leasing cheaper than buying the decor?
faqs.answer: Over the first season, leasing costs less because there is no capital purchase. Over five or more seasons the totals can come closer, but a purchase still carries annual setup, service, takedown and storage fees, plus the cost of replacing lighting and ornaments as they age. Leasing keeps the display fresh, moves breakage and storage to us and keeps the whole cost as one operating line. We show both numbers in the quote so you can decide.

faqs.question: What does a leased lobby tree program typically cost per season?
faqs.answer: As a typical range, a 9 ft fully decorated pre-lit lobby tree with setup, maintenance, removal and storage commonly starts around $1,500 per season. Atrium trees, accent trees, garland and planters build from there, and full hotel or mall programs run into five figures. Exterior leasing programs start from a few thousand for a storefront and run to tens of thousands for a plaza or campus. These are typical ranges, not quotes.

faqs.question: Can we change the design during a multi-year agreement?
faqs.answer: Yes. The lease covers the look, not a fixed set of boxes. Many clients keep the tree and lighting the same and refresh ribbon and ornament colours in year two or three, or add entrance garland and planters as budget allows. Changes are quoted at the agreed rates in the term. Because we store and refurbish the inventory, swapping a colour scheme is a warehouse job for us, not a purchase for you.

faqs.question: Who is responsible if leased decor is damaged or stolen?
faqs.answer: Normal wear, weather damage and failures are ours to fix at no charge; that is what maintenance on a lease means. Damage from a vehicle strike, vandalism or theft is handled under your property insurance in the same way as any other property of others on site, and we provide replacement values and certificates of insurance on request so your broker has what they need. We will tell you the values before you sign.

intro: Commercial holiday lighting installation and storage belong in the same program, because the way a display comes down decides how well it goes up next year. Takedown is scheduled after hours on a date you choose, so a lobby tree is gone before the first tenant arrives and an exterior crew with a lift is off the lot before the morning rush. Clips, cords, timers and mounts come down with the product. We leave the building and grounds as we found them and photograph anything we want you to see.

Over the summer, trees, garland and lighting are tested, repaired and refurbished so what goes up in October works on the first night. Returning clients get priority rebooking: your install and takedown dates are held before new work is scheduled. There is nothing for your building staff to carry, box or find room for. Install photos from the previous season are kept on file so the crew sets up to the same plan.

faqs.question: Is takedown and storage included or an extra charge?
faqs.answer: It is included in every program, leased or owned. The seasonal price covers removal in January, labelling, storage in our warehouse and refurbishment before the next install. The only exception is a client who wants product removed and stored outside the January window, which we schedule and quote individually.

faqs.question: When exactly do you take the lights down?
faqs.answer: In the first three weeks of January, on a date you choose. Hotels and offices usually want lobby trees gone in the first week once holiday traffic ends. Exterior rooflines and tree wraps come down through mid-January, weather permitting, since lift work pauses during ice storms and high wind. If you want lights left up for a January event or a winter festival, tell us and we schedule around it.

faqs.question: Do you take down lights that another company installed?
faqs.answer: Only as part of switching you to our program. We will remove and dispose of or return an old display when we are installing our own inventory in its place, and we price that into the first-year quote. We do not store or reinstall product we did not supply, because we cannot test or warranty it. Most clients switching to us let the old product go and start fresh under a lease.

faqs.question: What condition will our building be in after takedown?
faqs.answer: The same as before install. Clips, ties, cords, timers and mounts all come down with the decor. We do not leave hooks on columns or hardware on rooflines over the summer. Floors and finishes are protected during interior removal, and we photograph the site on the way out. If we notice anything, a loose piece of fascia or a cracked planter, we report it to you with a photo rather than leave it for you to find.

faqs.question: How do you make sure the same display goes back up next year?

h1: Seasonal maintenance and service, included on every program
eyebrow: No charge for any fault, all season
intro: Seasonal maintenance is included on every commercial holiday lighting and decor program we install, with no charge for any fault. A dark section on a roofline, a lobby tree with a band of lights out, a cone tree knocked over by a plow, a timer that lost its schedule after a power blip: you call or text, and we fix it. That is the standard, not a service tier.

We can promise this because everything we install is our own commercial-grade inventory. Crews carry spare strings, tree sections, plugs, clips, bows and timers, so most calls are fixed on the first visit rather than waiting on parts. Exterior service runs from the same bucket trucks and lifts as the install, so a third-storey roofline is as reachable in December as it was in November.

After a major wind or ice storm we check exposed properties without being asked, because the point of a commercial display is that it is on and complete every night of the season. Service visits are scheduled after hours wherever possible, and we respond to every request within one business day, usually the same day in December. Property managers get one number for every site on the program.

includes.title: Lighting faults
includes.body: A section out on a roofline, tree wrap or garland run is traced to the failed string, plug or fuse and replaced from stock on the truck. Pre-lit trees are wired in sections, so we swap the section rather than rewire the tree. Our commercial product uses the same connectors across the program, which keeps repairs quick.

includes.title: Timers, photocells and power
includes.body: Timers that lost their program after an outage are reset to your hours. Photocells that are shaded by snow or a new sign are repositioned. A tripped GFCI or breaker is traced to the cause, usually water in a connection, which is dried, re-taped and elevated. We leave a note of what changed.

includes.title: Physical damage
includes.body: Cone trees and planters knocked by plows or carts are reset and re-staked. Clips pulled by wind are replaced and the run re-tensioned. Ribbon and ornaments pulled loose in a lobby are re-tied or replaced. Tree wraps that have slipped are re-secured. Vehicle strikes and vandalism are documented with photos for your insurance.

includes.title: Storm checks
includes.body: After significant wind, ice or heavy snow we check exposed exterior programs, especially rooflines, porte-cochères and parking-lot trees, and fix anything that has moved or gone dark. You do not need to call. Lift work waits until wind and ice allow it to be done safely, and we tell you if there is a delay.

includes.title: Response times
includes.body: We respond to every service request within one business day, and in December most calls are handled the same day. Interior work is scheduled after hours with your concierge or security. Exterior work runs at night where lifts and traffic make that safer. High-visibility faults, such as a dark hotel entrance, are prioritised.

includes.title: One number, logged visits
includes.body: Property managers get one phone number for every site on their program. Each service visit is logged with what was found and what was done, and we send a short note with photos when it helps. At the end of the season you have a record of every issue and fix, which makes next year's planning easier.

process.title: Report the issue
process.body: Call or text 519-266-6796 or email with the property and a quick description. A photo from your phone helps us bring the right parts. Storm checks happen without a call on exposed properties.

process.body: The fault is corrected, the circuit is tested end to end and the timer or photocell is checked so the display comes on that evening. We look over the rest of the program while we are there.

process.title: Log and follow up
process.body: The visit is logged with what was found and fixed. If something points to a larger issue, such as an outlet that keeps tripping, we tell you so your electrician can look at it before it causes a dark night.

faqs.question: What happens when a strand of lights fails on our building?
faqs.answer: You call or text us and we schedule a visit, usually after hours and usually within a business day. The crew traces the dark section to the failed string, plug or fuse, replaces it from stock on the truck and tests the whole circuit before leaving. On a roofline or tree wrap the lift comes back. There is no charge, because maintenance is included on every program and the product is our own inventory.

faqs.question: Is seasonal maintenance really free, or is there a call-out fee?
faqs.answer: There is no call-out fee and no charge for parts or labour on any fault during the season. It is built into the program price, whether you lease the decor or own it under an annual service agreement with us. The only costs that fall outside are damage from a vehicle strike, vandalism or theft, which is usually a property insurance matter, and we document those with photos so your claim is straightforward.

faqs.question: Our lights are on a timer that keeps losing its schedule. Can you fix that?
faqs.answer: Yes. Mechanical and digital timers can lose their program after a power outage, and photocells can be shaded by snow, a new sign or a parked truck. We reset timers to your hours, reposition or replace photocells and check that the circuit is not tripping a GFCI, which is the most common cause of a display that is dark one night and fine the next. Water in a connection is usually the culprit, and we dry, re-tape and elevate it.

faqs.question: Do you check the display after a storm or do we have to call?
faqs.answer: We check exposed exterior programs after major wind, ice or heavy snow without being asked, because rooflines, porte-cochères and parking-lot trees take the most abuse. If something has moved or gone dark we fix it on that visit. Lift work waits until conditions are safe, and we tell you if that creates a delay. You are always welcome to call as well, especially if a specific area looks wrong.

faqs.question: How quickly do you respond to a service request in December?
faqs.answer: We respond to every request within one business day, and in December most are handled the same day because crews are already out across the region. High-visibility faults, such as a dark hotel entrance or a lobby tree with a section out, go to the top of the list. Interior visits are scheduled after hours with your concierge or security so tenants and guests do not see a crew on a ladder in the lobby.

h1: Custom displays, Santa sets, giant trees and animated light shows
eyebrow: Feature displays that draw a crowd
intro: Custom displays are the part of a commercial holiday program that people travel to see and photograph. We design and build Santa photo sets and mall villages for enclosed shopping centres, giant outdoor trees for plazas and town squares, lit sculptures and tunnels for atriums and animated pixel light shows synced to music for building facades and park pavilions, all from our own inventory.

Each display starts with the space and the crowd: where people enter, where the queue forms, where the photo gets taken and where the lift can set up overnight. Branded colour schemes are common, so a plaza's giant tree can carry the centre's colours and a hotel's entrance can match its brand standard without looking like a logo. We confirm colours on physical samples before anything is ordered.

Displays are built after hours with insured, WSIB-compliant crews, secured against tipping and wind, checked for clearances and exits, and put on timers. Maintenance is included for the season, which matters more for a display that thousands of people walk past each day than for anything else we install. January takedown and labelled storage are included. Everything we build is our own inventory, so we can warranty it.

includes.title: Santa photo sets
includes.body: Log-cabin and village-style Santa sets for enclosed malls and large lobbies, with a seating area, backdrop, fencing for the queue, decorated trees and a photo podium. We design the sightline for the camera first, then build around it. Sets are modular so they fit the court you have and store flat in January.

includes.title: Mall villages and centrepieces
includes.body: Lit village displays, sleigh features, lit birch forests, reindeer sculptures and planter centrepieces for atriums and concourses. Pieces are weighted and secured against curious kids and cleaning carts, and nothing blocks a fire exit, a sprinkler or a storefront entrance. Installs run overnight so the court opens on time.

includes.title: Giant outdoor trees
includes.body: Giant cone trees and large pre-lit outdoor trees for plaza courtyards, town squares and campus entrances, with a star topper and a lit base. Trees are engineered for wind, staked or ballasted and set back from plow routes. They are built from a lift overnight and sit on their own circuit with a timer or photocell.

includes.title: Animated pixel light shows
includes.body: Pixel LED mega trees, facade outlines, snowflakes and star displays synced to music, programmed for your building. Shows run on a schedule you set, with a static look between shows so the property is never dark. We handle controllers, power and the programming, and we can add tracks or themes year to year.

includes.title: Branded colour schemes
includes.body: Trees, lighting, ribbon and displays matched to a brand standard or a centre's identity: a specific blue on a facade, a plaza's signature red on the giant tree, a hotel's warm-white-and-gold across the lobby and porte-cochère. We confirm colours against samples before ordering so what goes up is what was approved.

includes.title: Tunnels, arches and photo moments
includes.body: Walk-through light tunnels and garland arches for lobbies, parks and courtyards, placed where people naturally stop for a photo. Structures are rated for the span, anchored and lit on timers. For public spaces we design clear widths and exits with your security or events team so the crowd moves safely.

process.title: Concept and site review

process.body: Maintenance is included at no charge all season. Shows are monitored and reprogrammed if you want a change. In January the display comes down, is inventoried and goes into labelled storage in our warehouse.

faqs.question: How much does a mall Santa set or village display cost?
faqs.answer: Custom displays are quoted from a site visit and a concept, so there is no list price. As a typical range, interior programs with themed displays run into five figures per season for atrium and mall work, and giant trees and pixel light shows for a plaza or campus are in the tens of thousands depending on size and show length. Leasing spreads that across seasons and includes service, takedown and storage. These are typical ranges, not quotes.

faqs.question: Can the display be built without closing the mall or the square?
faqs.answer: Yes. We build overnight after close and open the area each morning, so a large Santa set or village is usually a two- or three-night job with the court usable in between. Outdoor giant trees and pixel shows are built from a lift at night with cones and a spotter for traffic. We coordinate with your security, cleaning crews and events team so there are no surprises on the overnight schedule.

faqs.question: How does an animated pixel light show work?
faqs.answer: Pixel LED fixtures, such as a mega tree, facade outlines, snowflakes and stars, are wired to a controller that plays a programmed sequence synced to music. You choose the show schedule, for example every half hour from dusk to close, and the fixtures hold a static colour look between shows so the building is never dark. We supply and program the controllers, handle power and can add songs or themes year to year.

faqs.question: Can the display match our brand colours?
faqs.answer: Yes. We match lighting, ribbon, ornaments and display finishes to a brand standard or a centre's identity and confirm them on physical samples before ordering, because a blue on a screen and a blue on a facade at night are not the same thing. Branded schemes work best when they are used with restraint, for example your colour on the giant tree and warm white everywhere else, and we will say so if a scheme is heading toward looking like a sign.

faqs.question: What about safety, insurance and fire code for public displays?
faqs.answer: Displays in public spaces are secured against tipping and wind, built with clear widths and exits agreed with your security or events team, kept clear of sprinklers, pull stations and storefront entrances, and lit with low-draw LED on timers. Our crews are insured and WSIB-compliant and we provide certificates of insurance on request. Queue fencing and photo podiums are placed so lines do not block egress. Any display damage during the season is fixed at no charge.
